source.text: וַיֵּאָסְפ֤וּ כָל־הָעָם֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד אֶל־הָ֣רְח֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י שַֽׁעַר־הַמָּ֑יִם וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ לְעֶזְרָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֔ר לְהָבִ֗יא אֶת־סֵ֨פֶר֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered all the people as one man to the square that [was] before [the] gate of the waters; and they said to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of [the] law of Moses which commanded YHWH Israel.

en.L: And all the people gathered as one man to the square that [was] in front of the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Israel.
en.B: All the people gathered together as one to the square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded for Israel.
en.R: All the people came together as if they were one person. They met in the open square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra, the teacher of the law, to bring out the book of the law of Moses. This was the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Israel to obey.

decisions.choice: as one man: all together, with one purpose
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the whole people acting like a single person (Judges 20:1, 8; Ezra 3:1). The gathering was the people's own doing: they ask Ezra to bring the book, he does not summon them.

decisions.choice: the square before the Water Gate: an open public space on the east side of the city
decisions.reason: The Water Gate stood on the east side of Jerusalem, toward the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley (3:26; 12:37). A square near a gate was where people met and public business was done. Holding the reading there, not in the temple courts, let men and women alike attend (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the book of the law of Moses: the written teaching given through Moses
alternatives: the Torah, the five books of Moses
decisions.reason: The word for "book" means a written scroll. The law of Moses is the teaching the LORD gave Israel through Moses, written down (Deuteronomy 31:9-11, 24-26). The text does not say how much of the five books the scroll held, but what is read in verses 14-15 comes from Leviticus 23.

decisions.choice: Ezra, the teacher of the law
decisions.reason: As in Ezra 7:6, Readable explains the title "scribe": Ezra was a scholar who studied and taught the law, not only someone who wrote. Literal and Balanced keep "the scribe".

source.text: וַיָּבִ֣יא עֶזְרָ֣א הַ֠כֹּהֵן אֶֽת־הַתּוֹרָ֞ה לִפְנֵ֤י הַקָּהָל֙ מֵאִ֣ישׁ וְעַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה וְכֹ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין לִשְׁמֹ֑עַ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought Ezra the priest the law before the assembly, from man and to woman and every [one] understanding to hear, on day one of the month the seventh.

en.L: And Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both man and woman and everyone able to understand [what they would] hear, on day one of the seventh month.
en.B: So Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, men and women and all who could understand what they heard. It was the first day of the seventh month.
en.R: So Ezra the priest brought the book of the law to the whole crowd. Men and women were there, and everyone who was old enough to understand what was read. This was on the first day of the seventh month.

decisions.choice: the first day of the seventh month: a sacred day of rest and assembly
decisions.reason: The law makes the first day of the seventh month a day of rest and a holy assembly, marked by trumpet blasts (Leviticus 23:23-25; Numbers 29:1-6). The seventh month, Tishri, falls in September to October and also holds the Day of Atonement (tenth day) and the Festival of Booths (fifteenth day). Its first day began the season of festivals that this chapter goes on to keep (verses 14-18).

decisions.choice: man and woman and everyone who could understand: children old enough to follow were present too
decisions.reason: "From man to woman" is a Hebrew way of saying "both men and women". "Everyone who understands to hear" adds those who were able to follow what was read, most likely the older children (10:29; Deuteronomy 31:12 has men, women and little ones gather to hear the law).

decisions.choice: everyone who was old enough to understand
decisions.reason: Readable spells out who the phrase most likely means, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָא־בוֹ֩ לִפְנֵ֨י הָרְח֜וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀לִפְנֵ֣י שַֽׁעַר־הַמַּ֗יִם מִן־הָאוֹר֙ עַד־מַחֲצִ֣ית הַיּ֔וֹם נֶ֛גֶד הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַמְּבִינִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־סֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he read in it before the square that [was] before [the] gate of the waters from the light until [the] half of the day, before the men and the women and the understanding [ones]; and [the] ears of all the people [were] to the book of the law.

en.L: And he read from it in front of the square that [was] in front of the Water Gate from the light until the middle of the day, in front of the men and the women and those who could understand; and the ears of all the people [were turned] to the book of the law.
en.B: He read from it, facing the square in front of the Water Gate, from early morning until midday, before the men and women and those who could understand. And all the people listened closely to the book of the law.
en.R: Ezra read from the book from early morning until noon. He faced the square in front of the Water Gate. The men, the women and those who could understand were there. All the people listened carefully to the book of the law.

decisions.choice: from the light until the middle of the day: from daybreak to noon
decisions.reason: "The light" is the first light of morning. The reading lasted about six hours.

decisions.choice: the ears of all the people were to the book: they listened attentively
decisions.reason: To have one's ears turned to something is to listen with attention (Psalm 130:2). The phrase says the people kept listening through the whole long reading.

decisions.choice: read from it; listened closely
decisions.reason: The verb means to read aloud, as the setting makes plain. Readable names Ezra as the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to the verb.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֞ד עֶזְרָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֗ר עַֽל־מִגְדַּל־עֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ לַדָּבָר֒ וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֣ד אֶצְל֡וֹ מַתִּתְיָ֡ה וְשֶׁ֡מַע וַ֠עֲנָיָה וְאוּרִיָּ֧ה וְחִלְקִיָּ֛ה וּמַעֲשֵׂיָ֖ה עַל־יְמִינ֑וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאל֗וֹ פְּ֠דָיָה וּמִֽישָׁאֵ֧ל וּמַלְכִּיָּ֛ה וְחָשֻׁ֥ם וְחַשְׁבַּדָּ֖נָה זְכַרְיָ֥ה מְשֻׁלָּֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And stood Ezra the scribe on [a] tower of wood which they had made for the matter, and stood beside him Mattithiah and Shema and Anaiah and Uriah and Hilkiah and Maaseiah on his right; and from his left Pedaiah and Mishael and Malkijah and Hashum and Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, Meshullam.

en.L: And Ezra the scribe stood on a tower of wood which they had made for the purpose. And beside him stood Mattithiah and Shema and Anaiah and Uriah and Hilkiah and Maaseiah, on his right, and on his left Pedaiah and Mishael and Malkijah and Hashum and Hashbaddanah, Zechariah [and] Meshullam.
en.B: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that had been built for the occasion. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.
en.R: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this reading. Six men stood at his right side: Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah. Seven men stood at his left side: Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.

decisions.choice: a tower of wood: a raised wooden platform
decisions.reason: The word usually means a tower; here it is a high stand built so that Ezra could be seen and heard by the crowd (verse 5).

decisions.choice: thirteen men stood with Ezra, six on his right and seven on his left
decisions.reason: The text does not say who these men were. They were probably leaders of the people or priests standing with Ezra to show that the community stood behind the reading. Some of the names appear among the leaders who later seal the covenant (10:4-28).

decisions.choice: six men; seven men
decisions.reason: Readable counts the names, which the list itself gives, to make the long list easier to follow.

source.text: וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח עֶזְרָ֤א הַסֵּ֨פֶר֙ לְעֵינֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־מֵעַ֥ל כָּל־הָעָ֖ם הָיָ֑ה וּכְפִתְח֖וֹ עָֽמְד֥וּ כָל־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And opened Ezra the book to [the] eyes of all the people, for above all the people he was; and when he opened it stood all the people.

en.L: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
en.B: Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, since he stood above them all. And as he opened it, all the people stood up.
en.R: Ezra opened the book where all the people could see him, because he was standing higher than everyone else. As soon as he opened it, all the people stood up.

decisions.choice: the people stood when the book was opened: a sign of respect for God's word
decisions.reason: Standing honors the one who speaks. King Eglon rose from his seat when told he would hear a word from God (Judges 3:20), and the Levites call the people to stand and bless the LORD (9:5).

decisions.choice: the book: a scroll that is unrolled
decisions.reason: Books were scrolls; to "open" one was to unroll it to the place to be read.

source.text: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ עֶזְרָ֔א אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הַגָּד֑וֹל וַיַּֽעֲנ֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֜ם אָמֵ֤ן׀אָמֵן֙ בְּמֹ֣עַל יְדֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲוֻּ֛ לַיהוָ֖ה אַפַּ֥יִם אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And blessed Ezra YHWH the God the great; and answered all the people, Amen, amen, with [the] lifting of their hands; and they bowed and they worshiped YHWH [with] faces to the ground.

en.L: And Ezra blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the great God, and all the people answered, Amen, amen, with the lifting up of their hands. And they bowed and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with [their] faces to the ground.
en.B: Ezra blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the great God, and all the people lifted up their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with their faces to the ground.
en.R: Ezra praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the great God. All the people raised their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down low and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with their faces to the ground.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised
decisions.reason: When a person blesses God, the word means to praise him and give him thanks (9:5; Psalm 103:1).

decisions.choice: Amen, amen: "It is true", "So be it"
decisions.reason: Amen comes from a root meaning firm or sure. By saying it the people agreed to the praise and made it their own (Deuteronomy 27:15-26; 1 Chronicles 16:36). Saying it twice makes it stronger.

decisions.choice: lifted hands, bowing, faces to the ground: the body's posture in prayer and worship
decisions.reason: Lifting the hands is a gesture of prayer and praise (Psalm 28:2; 134:2). Bowing down with the face to the ground is the deepest sign of honor (Exodus 4:31; 2 Chronicles 7:3). The two verbs, "bowed" and "worshiped", are often paired; the second means to lay oneself low before someone.

source.text: וְיֵשׁ֡וּעַ וּבָנִ֡י וְשֵׁרֵ֥בְיָ֣ה׀יָמִ֡ין עַקּ֡וּב שַׁבְּתַ֣י׀הֽוֹדִיָּ֡ה מַעֲשֵׂיָ֡ה קְלִיטָ֣א עֲזַרְיָה֩ יוֹזָבָ֨ד חָנָ֤ן פְּלָאיָה֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מְבִינִ֥ים אֶת־הָעָ֖ם לַתּוֹרָ֑ה וְהָעָ֖ם עַל־עָמְדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jeshua and Bani and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites [were] causing the people to understand the law; and the people [were] on their standing.

en.L: And Jeshua and Bani and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites were helping the people to understand the law, while the people [stayed] in their places.
en.B: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah, the Levites, helped the people understand the law, while the people stayed where they stood.
en.R: The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah explained the law to the people. The people stayed standing in their places.

decisions.choice: "and the Levites": the named men are Levites
alternatives: the named men and also the other Levites
decisions.reason: The "and" before "the Levites" can join a further group to the list, or it can explain the list ("that is, the Levites"). Many of the names are known as Levites (Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Hodiah: 9:4-5; 10:10-14), so the second reading is likely; the ancient Greek and Latin translations read "and the Levites" without the joining word here. This reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: causing to understand: explaining
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative form of "understand" (verses 2-3, 8, 12). The Levites made the law clear to the people, perhaps by going among the groups after the reading and explaining it (verse 8). This was part of the Levites' charge to teach Israel (Deuteronomy 33:10; 2 Chronicles 17:7-9; 35:3).

decisions.choice: the people [were] on their standing: they stayed in their places
decisions.reason: The phrase means they remained standing where they were, as in verse 5.

source.text: וַֽיִּקְרְא֥וּ בַסֵּ֛פֶר בְּתוֹרַ֥ת הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מְפֹרָ֑שׁ וְשׂ֣וֹם שֶׂ֔כֶל וַיָּבִ֖ינוּ בַּמִּקְרָֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they read in the book, in the law of the God, explained, and giving sense, and they understood in the reading.

en.L: And they read in the book, in the law of God, clearly, and giving [the] sense, and they understood the reading.
en.B: They read from the book, from the law of God, clearly, and they gave the sense, so that the people understood what was read.
en.R: They read from the book of God's law and made it clear. They explained what it meant, so the people could understand what was being read.

decisions.choice: meforash: "clearly"; it may mean "with interpretation" or "translating"
decisions.reason: The word is a passive form of a verb meaning to make distinct or plain (Leviticus 24:12; Numbers 15:34). In this verse it can mean that the law was read clearly, distinctly; or that it was read with explanation, section by section. Jewish tradition took it to mean that the reading was translated into Aramaic, the common language of the Persian empire, which many returned exiles spoke (13:24 shows that some children could not speak Hebrew), and saw here the beginning of the Targums, the Aramaic translations read in the synagogue. The same word is used in Ezra 4:18 (in Aramaic) of a letter "read clearly" or "translated" before the king. "Clearly" is taken as the sense here, since every reading includes it; the next words, "giving the sense", show that explanation followed the reading in any case.

decisions.choice: they read: the Levites of verse 7 with Ezra
alternatives: Ezra alone, with the plural meaning "it was read"
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, so it most likely means Ezra and the Levites named in verse 7 together; the Hebrew plural can also be used without a definite subject ("it was read").

decisions.choice: giving the sense, and they understood the reading
decisions.reason: The word for "sense" means insight or good understanding. Reading alone was not enough; the meaning had to be made plain, so that the people understood. The verse sets out three steps: reading, explaining and understanding.

decisions.choice: They explained what it meant
decisions.reason: Readable turns "giving the sense" into a plain sentence and says "the people", whom the verb in the Hebrew implies.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נְחֶמְיָ֣ה ה֣וּא הַתִּרְשָׁ֡תָא וְעֶזְרָ֣א הַכֹּהֵ֣ן׀הַסֹּפֵ֡ר וְהַלְוִיִּם֩ הַמְּבִינִ֨ים אֶת־הָעָ֜ם לְכָל־הָעָ֗ם הַיּ֤וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ־הוּא֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם אַל־תִּֽתְאַבְּל֖וּ וְאַל־תִּבְכּ֑וּ כִּ֤י בוֹכִים֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם כְּשָׁמְעָ֖ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַתּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Nehemiah, he [is] the Tirshatha, and Ezra the priest, the scribe, and the Levites causing the people to understand, to all the people: The day is holy to YHWH your God; do not mourn and do not weep; for weeping [were] all the people as they heard the words of the law.

en.L: And Nehemiah, that is, the Tirshatha, and Ezra the priest [and] scribe, and the Levites who were helping the people to understand said to all the people, This day is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; do not mourn and do not weep. For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.
en.B: Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were teaching the people said to all the people, "This day is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not mourn and do not weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.
en.R: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher of the law, and the Levites who were explaining the law spoke to all the people. They said, "This is a holy day for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not be sad and do not cry." They said this because all the people were crying as they heard what the law said.

decisions.choice: the Tirshatha: a Persian title for the governor
decisions.reason: Tirshatha is a Persian title, probably meaning "his excellency", used for the governor of Judah (Ezra 2:63; Nehemiah 7:64, 69; 10:2). Nehemiah was appointed governor by the king (5:14).

decisions.choice: the day is holy to the LORD: a festival day set apart, not a day of mourning
decisions.reason: The first day of the seventh month was a sacred assembly (Leviticus 23:24-25; Numbers 29:1). A day holy to the LORD was to be kept with joy (Deuteronomy 16:14-15), so open grief did not fit it. The leaders do not say the people's sorrow is wrong; it is set aside for later (9:1-2).

decisions.choice: for all the people were weeping as they heard: the reason for the command
decisions.reason: The last clause tells why the leaders spoke: hearing the law showed the people how far they had fallen short of it, and they wept (compare 2 Kings 22:11-13). The verse does not say so in words, but chapter 9 confirms it.

decisions.choice: the governor
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the title Tirshatha, as Ezra 2:63 does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֡ם לְכוּ֩ אִכְל֨וּ מַשְׁמַנִּ֜ים וּשְׁת֣וּ מַֽמְתַקִּ֗ים וְשִׁלְח֤וּ מָנוֹת֙ לְאֵ֣ין נָכ֣וֹן ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־קָד֥וֹשׁ הַיּ֖וֹם לַאֲדֹנֵ֑ינוּ וְאַל־תֵּ֣עָצֵ֔בוּ כִּֽי־חֶדְוַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא מָֽעֻזְּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Go, eat fat [things] and drink sweet [things] and send portions to [him for whom] nothing is prepared for him, for holy [is] the day to our Lord; and do not be grieved, for the joy of YHWH, it [is] your stronghold.

en.L: And he said to them, Go, eat rich [food] and drink sweet [drinks], and send portions to [anyone for whom] nothing is prepared, for the day is holy to our Lord. And do not be grieved, for the joy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is your stronghold.
en.B: And he said to them, "Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to anyone who has nothing ready. For this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be grieved, for the joy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is your stronghold."
en.R: Then he told them, "Go home and enjoy a feast with good food and sweet drinks. Share some with people who have nothing ready to eat. This day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad. The joy that comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a strong place where you are safe."

decisions.choice: he said: most likely Nehemiah, or Ezra
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and names no one. Nehemiah is named first in verse 9, and Ezra leads the reading, so either could be meant. The text leaves him unnamed.

decisions.choice: your stronghold: a safe place, a fortress; often rendered "your strength"
decisions.reason: The word means a stronghold, a place to flee to for safety (Psalm 27:1; 31:3; 37:39; Isaiah 25:4). The familiar rendering "strength" catches part of it, but the picture is protection more than power: joy in God's goodness shelters the people when the law has made them grieve for their sins.

decisions.choice: the joy of the LORD: the joy that the LORD gives, or joy in the LORD
alternatives: the LORD's own joy over his people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase can mean the joy that comes from the LORD and is found in him, or the LORD's own joy over his people (Zephaniah 3:17). The festival setting (Deuteronomy 16:14-15) points to the people's rejoicing before the LORD; the first sense is the more likely.

decisions.choice: send portions to those with nothing prepared: sharing the festival meal with the poor
decisions.reason: Sending portions of food was part of keeping a feast (Esther 9:19, 22). The law asks Israel to rejoice at the festivals with the poor, the outsider, the orphan and the widow (Deuteronomy 16:11, 14).

decisions.choice: The joy that comes from the LORD is a strong place where you are safe
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold" in plain words and follows the more likely reading of "the joy of the LORD", which the decision on those words marks as uncertain.

source.text: וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם מַחְשִׁ֤ים לְכָל־הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר הַ֔סּוּ כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם קָדֹ֑שׁ וְאַל־תֵּעָצֵֽבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the Levites [were] quieting all the people, saying, Hush, for the day [is] holy, and do not be grieved.

en.L: And the Levites were calming all the people, saying, Be still, for the day is holy; and do not be grieved.
en.B: The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for this day is holy. Do not be grieved."
en.R: The Levites helped all the people to calm down. They said, "Be quiet now. This is a holy day. Do not be sad."

decisions.choice: quieting, Hush: calming the people's weeping
decisions.reason: The verb means to make silent or to still, and "Hush!" is the word one says to quiet someone (Judges 3:19; Amos 6:10). The Levites go among the people to calm their weeping (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Be still; Be quiet
decisions.reason: The interjection is rendered as a gentle command, since "Hush" can sound like scolding in English.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֜ם לֶאֱכֹ֤ל וְלִשְׁתּוֹת֙ וּלְשַׁלַּ֣ח מָנ֔וֹת וְלַעֲשׂ֖וֹת שִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה כִּ֤י הֵבִ֨ינוּ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹדִ֖יעוּ לָהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And went all the people to eat and to drink and to send portions and to make joy great, for they had understood the words which they had made known to them.

en.L: And all the people went to eat and to drink and to send portions and to make great rejoicing, for they had understood the words that they had made known to them.
en.B: So all the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions, and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
en.R: So all the people went off to eat and drink, to share food with others, and to celebrate with great joy. They did this because they now understood the words that had been explained to them.

decisions.choice: for they had understood: the reason for their joy
decisions.reason: The joy is grounded in understanding. The same word "understand" runs through the chapter (verses 2, 3, 7, 8, 9); now the people's understanding turns weeping into rejoicing.

decisions.choice: which they had made known to them: what the readers and Levites had taught
decisions.reason: The subject of "made known" is not named; it is Ezra and the Levites who read and explained the law (verses 7-8).

source.text: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֡י נֶאֶסְפוּ֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת לְכָל־הָעָ֗ם הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶל־עֶזְרָ֖א הַסֹּפֵ֑ר וּלְהַשְׂכִּ֖יל אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַתּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the day the second were gathered the heads of the fathers of all the people, the priests and the Levites, to Ezra the scribe, and [that was] to gain insight into the words of the law.

en.L: And on the second day the heads of the fathers of all the people, the priests and the Levites, were gathered to Ezra the scribe, to gain insight into the words of the law.
en.B: On the second day the heads of the families of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the law more closely.
en.R: On the next day the leaders of the families of all the people met with Ezra, the teacher of the law. The priests and the Levites came too. They wanted to understand the words of the law better.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here is short for "house of the fathers", the larger family or clan that traced its line to one ancestor (Ezra 1:5; 2:68). Their heads were the leaders of the community.

decisions.choice: to gain insight: to study closely and grasp the meaning
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for "sense" in verse 8. It means to look into something so as to understand it well. After the public reading, the leaders come to Ezra for closer study, so that they can teach their own households.

decisions.choice: the heads of the families; the leaders of the families
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "families" for "fathers", as the term table does for the house of the fathers.

source.text: וַֽיִּמְצְא֖וּ כָּת֣וּב בַּתּוֹרָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֩ יֵשְׁב֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל בַּסֻּכּ֛וֹת בֶּחָ֖ג בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they found written in the law which YHWH commanded by [the] hand of Moses that should dwell the sons of Israel in booths at the festival in the month the seventh,

en.L: And they found written in the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel should dwell in booths during the festival in the seventh month,
en.B: And they found written in the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were to live in booths during the festival of the seventh month,
en.R: In the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given through Moses, they found something written. It said that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} should live in shelters made of branches during the festival in the seventh month.

decisions.choice: living in booths at the festival of the seventh month: Leviticus 23:39-43
decisions.reason: The law sets the Festival of Booths on the fifteenth to the twenty-second day of the seventh month (Leviticus 23:34-36, 39-43; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). For seven days Israel was to live in booths, so that each generation would know that the LORD made their ancestors live in booths when he brought them out of Egypt (Leviticus 23:43). It also marked the end of the harvest.

decisions.choice: booths: shelters of branches
decisions.reason: The word means a rough shelter woven from branches and leaves, such as a watchman's hut in a field (Isaiah 1:8) or a shelter for cattle (Genesis 33:17). The older rendering "tabernacles" names the same festival.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through", by the agency of someone.

decisions.choice: shelters made of branches
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the booths were, as the next verse describes.

decisions.choice: the verse ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 15, which gives what they were to proclaim.

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יַשְׁמִ֗יעוּ וְיַעֲבִ֨ירוּ ק֥וֹל בְּכָל־עָרֵיהֶם֮ וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ צְא֣וּ הָהָ֗ר וְהָבִ֨יאוּ֙ עֲלֵי־זַ֨יִת֙ וַעֲלֵי־עֵ֣ץ שֶׁ֔מֶן וַעֲלֵ֤י הֲדַס֙ וַעֲלֵ֣י תְמָרִ֔ים וַעֲלֵ֖י עֵ֣ץ עָבֹ֑ת לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת סֻכֹּ֖ת כַּכָּתֽוּב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and that they should proclaim and cause a voice to pass in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, Go out to the mountain and bring leaves of olive and leaves of tree of oil and leaves of myrtle and leaves of palms and leaves of tree [with] thick [boughs] to make booths, as [is] written.

en.L: and that they should proclaim and spread [the] word in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, Go out to the hill country and bring branches of olive and branches of oil tree and branches of myrtle and branches of palms and branches of leafy trees, to make booths, as [it is] written.
en.B: and that they should announce it and spread the word in all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills and bring branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm and other leafy trees to make booths, as it is written."
en.R: It also said that they should announce a message in all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills. Bring back branches from olive trees, wild olive trees, myrtle trees, palm trees and other trees with thick leaves. Use them to make shelters, just as the law says."

decisions.choice: tree of oil: probably the wild olive
alternatives: oleaster, a shrub with oil-bearing fruit
decisions.reason: "Tree of oil" is a different tree from the olive named just before it. It is perhaps the wild olive or oleaster, or a resinous tree such as a pine; the same name is used for the wood of the cherubim in Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:23) and for a tree of the wilderness (Isaiah 41:19). The identification is not certain.

decisions.choice: as it is written: the command of Leviticus 23:40
decisions.reason: Leviticus 23:40 tells Israel to take fruit of splendid trees, palm fronds, boughs of leafy trees and willows of the brook, and to rejoice. The list here is not word for word the same; it applies the command to the trees that grew in the hills around Jerusalem. "As it is written" refers to the command to make booths from branches.

decisions.choice: proclaim and cause a voice to pass: send an announcement throughout the land
decisions.reason: To "cause a voice to pass" is to have a message carried from place to place (Exodus 36:6; Ezra 1:1; 10:7).

decisions.choice: branches
decisions.reason: The word means leaves or foliage; for building booths it means leafy branches. Literal keeps "leaves".

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֣וּ הָעָם֮ וַיָּבִיאוּ֒ וַיַּעֲשׂוּ֩ לָהֶ֨ם סֻכּ֜וֹת אִ֤ישׁ עַל־גַּגּוֹ֙ וּבְחַצְרֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְחַצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבִרְחוֹב֙ שַׁ֣עַר הַמַּ֔יִם וּבִרְח֖וֹב שַׁ֥עַר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the people and brought and made for themselves booths, each on his roof and in their courtyards and in [the] courtyards of [the] house of the God and in [the] square of [the] gate of the waters and in [the] square of [the] gate of Ephraim.

en.L: And the people went out and brought [them] and made booths for themselves, each on his roof and in their courtyards and in the courtyards of the house of God and in the square of the Water Gate and in the square of the Gate of Ephraim.
en.B: So the people went out and brought the branches and made booths for themselves, each on their own roof, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of the house of God, in the square by the Water Gate, and in the square by the Gate of Ephraim.
en.R: So the people went out and brought back branches. They made shelters for themselves. Some built them on the flat roofs of their houses, some in their yards and some in the courtyards of God's temple. Others built them in the square by the Water Gate and in the square by the Gate of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: each on his roof: the flat roofs of houses
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs used as living space (Deuteronomy 22:8; 1 Samuel 9:25-26), so a booth could be set up there.

decisions.choice: the Gate of Ephraim: a gate in the north wall
decisions.reason: The Gate of Ephraim faced north toward the land of Ephraim (2 Kings 14:13; Nehemiah 12:39). With the Water Gate on the east, it shows booths were put up across the city.

decisions.choice: each on their own roof
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each ... his" means every household, men and women alike; Balanced uses the inclusive form, which is already plain English, so no setting is needed. Literal keeps "his". Readable rephrases.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֣וּ כָֽל־הַ֠קָּהָל הַשָּׁבִ֨ים מִן־הַשְּׁבִ֥י׀סֻכּוֹת֮ וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ בַסֻּכּוֹת֒ כִּ֣י לֹֽא־עָשׂ֡וּ מִימֵי֩ יֵשׁ֨וּעַ בִּן־נ֥וּן כֵּן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַתְּהִ֥י שִׂמְחָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And made all the assembly, the returning [ones] from the captivity, booths, and they dwelt in [the] booths; for not had done since [the] days of Jeshua son of Nun so the sons of Israel until the day the that. And there was joy very great.

en.L: And all the assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and dwelt in the booths, for since the days of Jeshua son of Nun until that day the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had not done so. And there was very great joy.
en.B: The whole assembly of those who had come back from captivity made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not done this. And there was very great joy.
en.R: The whole community of people who had come back from exile made shelters and lived in them. the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not celebrated like this since the time of Joshua son of Nun. Everyone was full of joy.

decisions.choice: had not done so since the days of Joshua: not with booths kept like this by all the people
decisions.reason: The festival had been kept since Joshua's time (1 Kings 8:2, 65; 2 Chronicles 8:13; Ezra 3:4). What had not been done "so" was this: the whole people living in booths as the law commands, or keeping it with such joy and with such care for the written law. Similar words are said of the Passover under Josiah (2 Kings 23:22; 2 Chronicles 35:18).

decisions.choice: Jeshua son of Nun: Joshua, Moses' successor
decisions.reason: Jeshua is the later form of the name Joshua (Ezra 2:2; 3:2). The son of Nun is Joshua who led Israel into the land (Joshua 1:1).

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the familiar form of the name so readers recognize Moses' successor; Literal keeps Jeshua as the text spells it.

decisions.choice: exile
decisions.reason: Readable says "exile", the plainer word for the captivity in Babylon.

source.text: וַ֠יִּקְרָא בְּסֵ֨פֶר תּוֹרַ֤ת הָאֱלֹהִים֙ י֣וֹם׀בְּי֔וֹם מִן־הַיּוֹם֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הָאַחֲר֑וֹן וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־חָג֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וּבַיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֛י עֲצֶ֖רֶת כַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he read in [the] book of [the] law of the God day by day, from the day the first until the day the last; and they kept [the] festival seven days, and on the day the eighth [was] a solemn assembly according to the rule.

en.L: And he read from the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day to the last day. And they kept the festival seven days, and on the eighth day [there was] a solemn assembly, according to the rule.
en.B: Day after day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the book of the law of God. They kept the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, as the law required.
en.R: Ezra read from the book of God's law every day, from the first day of the festival to the last. The people celebrated the festival for seven days. On the eighth day they gathered for a special closing meeting, as the law said they should.

decisions.choice: he read: Ezra
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and names no subject; Ezra is the reader throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: reading the law day by day at the festival: Deuteronomy 31:10-13
decisions.reason: Moses commanded that every seventh year, at the Festival of Booths, the law be read before all Israel, men, women and children (Deuteronomy 31:10-13). Here it is read every day of the festival.

decisions.choice: solemn assembly: the closing gathering on the eighth day
decisions.reason: The word means a sacred assembly, a day when work stops; the law sets one on the eighth day of the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:36; Numbers 29:35).

decisions.choice: a special closing meeting
decisions.reason: Readable explains "solemn assembly" as the gathering that closed the festival.
